record.paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures on Rational Systems in Three Dimensions
record.original_question: Assume alpha, beta, and gamma are in [0, infinity). For the recurrence z_{n+1} = (alpha + beta z_n + gamma z_{n-1})/z_{n-2}, for n = 0, 1, ..., is every positive solution bounded if and only if beta = gamma?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in[0,\infty)$ and consider the third-order rational difference equation
$$z_{n+1}=\frac{\alpha+\beta z_n+\gamma z_{n-1}}{z_{n-2}},\qquad n=0,1,2,\dots,$$
with positive initial conditions $z_{-2},z_{-1},z_0\in(0,\infty)$. A solution $(z_n)_{n\ge -2}$ is called bounded if $\sup_{n\ge -2}z_n<\infty$. Determine whether the following equivalence holds: every positive solution of the equation is bounded if and only if $\beta=\gamma$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published resolution of this specific boundedness equivalence for the three-dimensional rational recurrence $z_{n+1}=(\alpha+\beta z_n+\gamma z_{n-1})/z_{n-2}$. While the broader program on boundedness of rational difference equations (Camouzis–Ladas and collaborators) has resolved many cases, no clear evidence was found confirming or refuting this particular conjecture, so the status is recorded as unknown.

status_evidence.snippet: Collection of open problems and conjectures on three-dimensional rational systems including boundedness conjectures.
status_evidence.claim: The boundedness question for this third-order rational recurrence is posed as an open conjecture.
